findings.title: Weak or absent account password policy
findings.description: The IAM account password policy is the baseline for human credentials. A short minimum length, missing character-class requirements, or disabled password-reuse prevention weakens every console login in the account.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy minimum length below 14
findings.description: The account password policy allows passwords shorter than 14 characters. Short minimum lengths make console passwords far easier to brute-force. Set minimum_password_length to 14 or more.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy does not require uppercase characters
findings.description: The account password policy does not require uppercase letters, shrinking the password search space. Set require_uppercase_characters to true.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy does not require numbers
findings.description: The account password policy does not require numeric characters, shrinking the password search space. Set require_numbers to true.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy does not require symbols
findings.description: The account password policy does not require symbol characters, shrinking the password search space. Set require_symbols to true.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy allows password reuse
findings.description: The account password policy does not prevent password reuse (absent or 0), so users can cycle back to old (possibly compromised) passwords. Set password_reuse_prevention to a positive value (24 recommended by CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark).
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password maximum age too long or disabled
findings.description: The account password policy lets passwords live longer than 90 days (or never expire when set to 0), widening the window in which a compromised password stays useful. Set max_password_age between 1 and 90.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM account has no alias
findings.description: No aws_iam_account_alias is defined, so the account is only identifiable by its numeric ID in the console sign-in URL and in audit trails. A memorable alias reduces the risk of operating in the wrong account.
findings.evidence: account_alias = absent (AWS default: numeric account ID only)
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: IAM password policy allows reset after expiry
findings.description: hard_expiry is disabled, so users can set a new password after their password has expired instead of being forced through the administrative reset flow. Enable hard_expiry for stricter expired-password handling.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: EBS volume encrypted with AWS-managed key, no customer-managed key
findings.description: This EBS volume is encrypted (encrypted = true) with the AWS-managed key instead of a customer-managed KMS key: no kms_key_id is set, so the volume uses the account default EBS key. A CMK gives you key rotation control, grants, CloudTrail audit of key use, and the ability to disable or delete the key. Set kms_key_id to a customer-managed key. (If the account default EBS key is itself a CMK, this is a false positive — see AEGIS-AWS-786 for the account-default control.) Unencrypted volumes are AEGIS-AWS-009's job and are not reported here.
findings.expected: kms_key_id set to a customer-managed KMS key
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.
